claim: ER4 Euribor is the largest single cost item for v5
evidence: After the ER4 correction (0.339 bp), ER4 costs 0.080 %/yr at L2 from 1990 and ranks 5th. The largest is IR4 (ASX 90-day bank bill) at 0.134 %/yr, then PA1 0.099, NO1 Curncy 0.093 and NG1 0.086. From 2010, IR4 0.141 and ER4 0.120. The ER4 correction saves about 0.11 pt/yr of v5 cost.

claim: The L1 gap in 2020-2021 (86->49, 36->16) mostly comes from CUA1
evidence: v5, lag 1, bp costs. In 2020, dropping only SCO1 gives 86.4->59.6 % and dropping only CUA1 gives 79.2 %, so iron ore SCO1 drives the 2020 gap. In 2021, dropping only CUA1 gives 36.4->20.7 % and dropping only SCO1 gives 29.0 %, so CUA1 drives 2021. From 2010, each market alone is worth about 0.07 Sharpe and 1.6 pt of CAGR.

claim: In 2023-07->2026-07 L2 > L1 because CUA1/SCO1 lost money and the lag helped slightly
evidence: The lag effect on CAGR is +0.17/+0.09/0.00/+0.03/-0.23 pt for v1..v5, essentially nil and negative for v5. The window gap comes from dropping CUA1/SCO1 (+1.1/+1.5/+1.7/+2.4/+2.6 pt) and from real costs (+0.1 to +0.2). The cash rule takes back -0.9 to -1.0 pt.

claim: Ranking v5>=v4>v3>v2>>v1 holds at every level over the long periods
evidence: This holds from 1990, 2000 and 2010. At L2 from 2015, v3 is at or above v4: CAGR 4.20 vs 4.14 %, Sharpe 0.2025 vs 0.1992. At L1 from 2010, the Sharpe of v4 and v5 is tied (0.5412 vs 0.5411).

claim: Costs in the 1990s were about twice today's in bp: 4.0 %/yr average 1990-2026 vs 2.1
evidence: Under X1 (constant USD per contract), the 1990-2026 AVERAGE is 1.9x (4.01 vs 2.11 %/yr). By decade the ratio is about 3x in the 1990s (6.7 vs 2.2), 1.9x in the 2000s (3.5 vs 1.8) and 1.2x from 2010 (2.67 vs 2.21). X1 keeps today's multipliers, which overstates 1990s equity-index bp costs (the big contracts then were 5-10x larger) and ignores the higher commissions of that era. Treat it as an order of magnitude.

claim: Standard equity, bond and STIR contracts cost much less than 1 bp
evidence: Median real cost per side vs the bp model, 82 markets: equities 0.77 vs 1.0, bonds 0.73 vs 1.0, FX 0.80 vs 1.0, STIR 0.37 vs 0.5, metals 0.91 vs 2.0, energy 1.54 vs 2.0, agriculture 4.08 vs 4.0. So costs are about 20-30 % below the model, not 'much less'. Real costs total 2.11 vs 2.46 %/yr for v5.
Arithmetic accrual is 2.72 %/yr. The published money-market CAGR is 2.76 %.
